title: Continental-lock routing: tenant allowlist adapter + emergency passthrough
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Some enterprise customers require strict continental residency (EU-only) for inference, while others need temporary exemptions (allowlist) or emergency passthrough when regional capacity is depleted. Current routing system lacks a tenant-scoped adapter that can apply allowlists/denylists, surface precedence clearly, and trigger a safe emergency passthrough with audit logging and SLO-aware degradations.

Goal: Implement a tenant-scoped Continental Lock Adapter (CLA) that evaluates tenant policies (continental residency requirement, per-tenant allowlist/denylist of regions or routes), enforces routing decisions, and coordinates safe fallback behaviors: -- hard block (reject) for true residency violations, -- soft fallback to EU-only compatible model variants, or -- emergency passthrough to non-EU route only when customer has explicitly allowed temporary escape and after operator-approved escalation. The adapter must: 1) be pluggable into the Smart Router pipeline, 2) expose policy evaluation traces to Console, 3) emit audit events to the compliance topic, and 4) respect Dedicated/Private deployment constraints.

Non-goals: this ticket does not implement UI for editing allowlists, ledger billing changes, or long-term policy authoring language; it implements the runtime enforcement and a lightweight API for tenant policy lookup.
acceptance_criteria: Tenant policy lookup API returns continental_lock: {enabled:true|false, allowed_regions:[...], emergency_passthrough_allowed:true|false}
Smart Router consults CLA and marks each request with routing_decision and compliance_flag in trace headers
Requests violating hard residency produce 403 with explicit compliance_code and create an audit entry in compliance-topic with tenant_id, request_id, route, and decision
Soft fallback routes to pre-approved EU-only model variants with KV-cache invalidation when variant switching occurs

Emergency passthrough only permitted when tenant policy has emergency_passthrough_allowed=true and operator-override flag is set; passthrough writes a high-fidelity audit record and tags session with 'escalation_id'
End-to-end tests demonstrating policy precedence: tenant allowlist overrides org-wide denylist when configured for the tenant
Console shows percentage of requests affected by continental-lock in the last 24/7 and an alert when passthrough rate > 0.1% of total requests for a tenant
decisions: Tenant allowlist has higher precedence than org-level denylist to enable hosted exceptions for enterprise customers
Hard residency violations will be explicit rejects (403) rather than transparent routing to EU variants unless tenant configured soft_fallback
Emergency passthrough requires two signals: tenant policy flag AND operator-override; passthrough is timeboxed and must include escalation_id for auditability
KV-caches keyed must include 'continental_lock_version' to prevent cache contamination across variant switches
tradeoffs: Strict enforcement maximizes compliance but increases failure surface and potential customer errors. Allowing passthrough reduces outages but increases audit volume and legal surface; we mitigate via strict operator controls, short TTLs on passthrough, and immediate customer notification hooks.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Unit + integration tests; deploy CLA behind feature flag to runtime staging and enable for 2 internal tenants (canary) for 1 week. Phase 2: Open beta for security/revenue customers with policy configured; monitor alerting and audit topics. Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 100% tenants with continental_lock policy present; default to disabled for tenants without policy. Use canary weights: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%.
testing_plan: Automated: policy-service mock returning combinations (hard-block, soft-fallback, passthrough) and asserting router behavior. Integration: end-to-end across ingress, router, model-variant switch, KV-cache invalidation. Chaos: simulate EU capacity exhaustion and validate emergency passthrough gating and audit records. Compliance tests: synthetic tenant requests with residency flags to ensure rejects and audit logs are created.
monitoring: New metrics: continental_lock.requests_total, continental_lock.rejected_total, continental_lock.passthrough_total, continental_lock.fallback_total. Traces include routing_decision and compliance_flag. Alerts: passthrough_rate_per_tenant > 0.1% (P1), rejected_rate increase > 5x baseline (P2). Audit topic retention 1 year for compliance review.
